Hades set up golden benchmark for rogue-lite games for good reasons. At the beginning I was very skeptical due its action genre that is not my usual cup of tea - and be honest I am also quite bad at it. But I still gave it a try... and than found how captivating it is. The story, the characters, the relations that develop and upgrade every run, alongside a rewarding meta progression system and different weapons... So I dived in. After initial runs and noob deaths I started improving and progress further and further. Started weapon upgrades, started discovering various skill combos and shaping character during the run alongside my clumsy reflexes... Took me 73 attempts for master everything enough to reach the game end.... but that was just another sort of beginning.. another 20-30 runs for true ending where you see eyour father from different light.. and after 137 runs I have finally unlocked all game achievements which come alongisde wraping all game stories (amazing at this point there are still new and new dialogues, but its starting to be bit too much for one game) Great experience, if some game should be evaluated as the best roguelite, it is Hades.

I played Cyberpunk 2077 at launch on PC, and yeah, it was buggy. To be fair, my experience back then wasn't quite the disaster everyone made it out to be, and I still enjoyed my time with it. But compared to where the game is today, it just wasn't ready to ship. Between the 2.0 overhaul and Phantom Liberty, CD Projekt Red has turned this into the game it always should have been. Night City is still one of the most atmospheric open worlds ever built, the reworked systems finally feel right, and Phantom Liberty is easily one of the best expansions in years. If you bounced off it at launch, this is the time to come back.

Please, if you can buy this game, i beg you to do it. I can’t put into words how good this game is. It is not perfect, the start was VERY rough, but in 2026, it is one of if not the best game you can play. Depends on what you like. -RPG elements : Not the most fleshed out, after all you are playing as your V and not a completely made-up character. Still, they’re very, very good. Also it‘s important to mention that this decision opened many great possibilities in the game development that otherwise wouldn’t be possible. -Combat : I would say a benchmark. The way you can customize your fighting style to what you want to do is ridiculous. Everyone can find their style. -Visuals, graphics : THE benchmark. Demanding, of course, but in 2026, doable. And stunning. The game is extremely beautiful. -The story, worldbuilding : This is the best part of the game by a longshot, and that’s saying something. The game treats you like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ adult for once, and you go through so many difficult, nail-biting, decisions that genuinely make you question who you are as a person. Not only is it very entertaining and downright inspirational, but very believable as well. You genuinely feel like a part of the story that is happening, somewhere, not so far away. Overall, i have not played a better game in my life. And honestly? I’m pretty sure that if CDPR doesn’t knock it out the park with the Witcher 4 or project Orion, i’ll never will :)

So far, I've gotten all achievements in Hades. I've died many times, I've raged a bit fewer times. But I learnt to love the loop of trying again, and again, and again. The gameplay loop is addictive, the story is immaculate, the artstyle is perfection, the accessibility settings from what I've seen are well made, but what takes the cake is the VA work. The entire cast has killed it, through and through, the entire dev team was absolutely a well oiled machine to make such an amazing piece of art. Just as much praise as everything else, the OPTIMIZIATION of this game. OH MY GODS. If you have what today would be considered a low-end rig or laptop, you're good! While Hades might not have too many options to change visuals compared to other games, it doesn't need it. It is buttery smooth, and it ran perfectly on a family PC as old as dirt that was way, way worse than the laptop I have now (specs attached). All my praises to the coders that worked on this! A friend of mine gifted me Hades 2 not too long ago, and I've been grinding the rest of achievements in this game before touching the second, and Heavens it's been worth it. I will still keep playing, there's yet more to do, stories to listen to, and so, so many more times to die. Absolutely worth every cent, if it's on sale, get it immediately then get it for your friends that don't have it. Even if you don't like roguelikes and are only interested in a good story, there's an option to make the game way easier for you to enjoy the story basically on its own! Go escape the underworld, I seriously could not recommend it enough.

One Ring made by the evil lord Sauron Hidetaka Miyazaki, One Ring to rule them all, One Ring to find them, One Ring to bring them all and in the darkness bind them, In the Land of Japanese software development warehouse building where Shadows lie. Elden Ring is not worth your time due to the profound curse placed upon the game's core design by the evil man who made it. The game aims at being infinitely replayable, but each of its assets is designed in a narrow fashion - so much so that the world does not feel as open as it is rather episodic. Each and every instance in the game is instrumented to be seen and encountered in a specific way which makes the experience of world exploration predictable and less exciting after playing for the first time. The dificulty ranges of the various explorable regions of the game world are awfully imballanced, so much so that it's less enjoyable to avoid choosing a linear path through the game on later playthroughs. The game world's incredibly size makes this issue even more frustrating - in order to experience something new on a subsequent playthrough, the player has to cross massive distances which are increasingly less and less aproachable the further he is from the starting point, ultimately discouraging exploration and narrowing the game experience to a single, most optimalized path of progression. There are only so many ways to reexperience the game's world without being severely discouraged and punished. And so ultimately, the game world's size and the quantity of its assets is severely nullified as the various paths to approach them are tragically so very limited. The game's world becomes eventually too predictable and the premise of experiencing the game in a fresh way nonexistent, which is not fun. Let it be pronounced and heard, Elden Ring could be legendary, but it is not, and won't be, unless FromSoftware developpers cease to practice the habit of forgetting a game once it's been created, despite the quantity of bothersome features still present and still widely acknowledged. One may recall the pathos of never properly finishing Lost Izalith in their previous game Dark Souls, an area of the game so very unique and all the more so disappointing for being critically underdevelopped. I feel very simillar about Elden Ring. As a former world of warcraft player, I see fit to pronounce a variety of ideas which could severely improve the experience of Elden Ring if they were ever developped, as they are present in that particular game, and although a very different game at that, still possesing a massive world and the spirit of an rpg game. Those ideas would be: There should be a variety of start points in Elden Ring, or at the very least, it should be possible to cross into other regions of the game from Limgrave without being stupefied and severely punished as much as is the case now. There should be more low level regions surrounding Limgrave so as to increase replayability and the possibilities of exploration on future playthroughs. And yes, despite the existence of various teleportation chests in Limgrave, the fact that the places you are sent to are completely above Limgrave's difficulty makes them less relevant as a travel feature. There is not enough enemy variety at each of the game's various places - an occasional "rare enemy spawn" or the promise of a "rare item drop" would be a solution to this issue. And lastly, there should be more paths connecting the various regions and places of the Elden Ring world and more accessible ways to connect the game's many features. In conclusion, Elden Ring nowhere near as fun as enjoyable after the first couple of playthroughs, it becomes stale and predictable rather too fast, and that is a completely nonsensical feature for a game of such high ambition and such quantity of the game's features.
